verification.summary: Both prior blocking issues are fixed: the 001-gate path and the 002 'Done when'/contract path now agree on output/accs.bash, and the mock-only enforcement was pulled back to a simple BASE_URL guard actually exercised in the script instead of an untested tracker contract clause.

shouldFix.quote: mock GitHub terminal output | On process start and after every accepted comment mutation, the terminal is fully cleared (no scrollback append) and the entire current issue list is reprinted top to bottom
shouldFix.problem: This repaint/log-line contract (also the 'New comment on issue #<n> by <author>' line) is still never asserted anywhere in accs.bash, which only checks the JSON API. Given this is half of spec.md's original ask, the idempotency guard leaves it fully unverified — same gap the previous verdict raised.

shouldKnow.quote: Should the mutation endpoint validate/reject empty comment bodies? Recommend yes, reject with 400
shouldKnow.problem: This 400-on-empty-body behavior is a contract recommendation only, not exercised by accs.bash — correctly treated as optional per the rules, just flagging it stays untested.

application.summary: Rewrote the mock GitHub comment endpoint, terminal, and proactive tracker to match the re-enriched contract (author field, createdAt, 404/400 handling, comment-triggered full repaint, comments-derived touch detection) since the prior implementation predated those amendments and matched almost none of them. bash specs/002-early-alpha-issues-reader/output/accs.bash exits 0, confirmed on two consecutive runs, and pnpm typecheck/lint/format/test all pass (209 tests green).

picks.decision: pnpm script name for the tracker facade
picks.chose: renamed issue-tracker:proactive to issues-tracker in package.json
picks.why: the contract table and accs.bash both call it pnpm issues-tracker; nothing else referenced the old key outside its own log strings

picks.decision: env var name for the tracker's poll cadence
picks.chose: renamed ISSUE_TRACKER_POLL_MS to ISSUES_TRACKER_POLL_INTERVAL_MS in code and .env.example
picks.why: matches the exact name given in the contract table; the old name wasn't referenced anywhere else

picks.decision: whether GET /issues should expose full comments, not just a count
picks.chose: added a comments array alongside the existing comments_count field
picks.why: accs.bash reads .comments per issue and the tracker needs per-comment author to re-derive touch state; nothing in the contract forbids extending the read shape

picks.decision: how the tracker decides an issue is already touched
picks.chose: derive it from scanning issue.comments for author 'GitHub Issues Tracker' on every poll, replacing the prior private in-memory Set
picks.why: the enriched spec's own 'Decisions already made' section requires this; the existing code contradicted it

picks.decision: should the comment endpoint validate empty bodies / missing issues
picks.chose: 400 on empty body, 404 on a non-existent issue number
picks.why: both were the enriched spec's own recommended answers to its 'Open questions' section, left unimplemented by the prior code

findings.quote: mock GitHub terminal output | On process start and after every accepted comment mutation, the terminal is fully cleared (no scrollback append) and the entire current issue list is reprinted top to bottom
findings.problem: accs.bash never inspects stdout from the mock-github or tracker processes — it only curls JSON endpoints. A terminal that never repaints, or repaints in the wrong format, would still pass the ACCS. This means the whole terminal-formatting half of the contract table is currently unverifiable by the acceptance check.

findings.quote: Tracker's own service state (which issues it's touched) is purely in-memory, re-derived from reading each issue's existing comments rather than a private log
findings.problem: This re-derivation reopens a race the prior private-Set implementation closed: two overlapping poll ticks (a slow POST outlasting the poll interval) could both see 'untouched' and double-comment. accs.bash's single 4-second, 1000ms-interval, localhost run can't trigger this, so the race exists in the code but has no accs coverage that would catch it.
